name: file-access-guard-prose
body:
The file-access prose of the distributed agents and the agent-builder template. Four distributed agent prompts — `spec-review.md`, `spec-writer.md`, `plan-writer.md`, `plan-review.md` — carry a `## File access (strict)` section whose "you may read any file" line contradicts the frontmatter read-guard; this component rewrites that section in each to state the rule plainly (graph state is reached only through the apg tools the agent actually holds; never read those node/transient files directly; ordinary source files behind code FQNs stay readable with `read`, all without naming the graph-state filesystem paths). It also extends `agent-builder.md`'s "Permission shape common to every generated agent" list and its step-6 verify checklist so every generated agent carries the same positive rule, not just the permission deny.

This is a markdown-prompt-text change only. The `.md` files are not scanned code; they are embedded into the binary at compile time via `include_str!` (the AGENTS constant in src/main.rs) and written to disk by `apg.install_suite` (src/main.rs:769). No Rust control flow and no observable CLI behavior changes.

Anchoring (delivery, not behavior): because markdown has no code-graph node, the coverage spine anchors to the Rust that embeds and delivers the templates — `apg.main` (the `include_str!` embedding consts) and `apg.install_suite` (the install path that writes them). These are the documented workaround per `solution.note.embedded-template-anchor` / `solution.note.markdown-anchoring`: a `.md` implemented-by target would fail write-time as drift. The plan therefore carries a delivery task with `modifies apg.install_suite` as the embedding/delivery anchor; it claims the existing embedding/install path, and no fake behavior change to `apg.main` is claimed.

The spine also reaches `solution.container.agent-install` (`apg.cmd_init`, `apg.install_suite`) through `domain.entity.agent-prose` / `domain.entity.permission-grant` (the requirement `read-guard-prose` and its children drive those entities). `agent-install` is the pre-existing `apg init` install/delivery path — it embeds and installs the same templates — so the plan claims its anchors on the same delivery-anchor basis. That coverage reach is intentional and explained, not an accidental demand. See `requirements.note.file-access-guard-coverage-anchoring`.
